chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Kinani, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when he ascended the pulpit, would say: 'It is befitting for the Muslim to avoid establishing brotherhood with three: the immoral (al-majin), the foolish (al-ahmaq), and the liar (al-kazzab).'

As for the immoral: he adorns his deed for you, and loves that you be like him, and he does not assist you in the affairs of your religion and hereafter; and associating with him is aloofness and hardness of heart, and his entry and exit upon you is a disgrace.

And as for the foolish: he does not indicate good to you, nor is he hoped for to ward off evil from you, even if he exerts himself; and perhaps he intends your benefit but harms you. Thus, his death is better than his life, his silence better than his speech, and his distance better than his nearness.

And as for the liar: life is not pleasant with him. He transmits your narration and transmits the narration to you. Whenever he exhausts one story, he stretches it with another, to the extent that when he narrates with the truth, he is not believed; and he incites enmity among people, causing grudges to grow in the chests.
Therefore, fear Allah and look out for yourselves.

key_terms.السَّخَائِمَ: Grudges or deep-seated enmity in the hearts.
key_terms.الْأَحْمَقُ: The foolish person who lacks wisdom, cannot effectively convey good or ward off evil, and whose presence may be more harmful than beneficial.
key_terms.الْكَذَّابُ: The liar who constantly narrates stories, exaggerates, and causes people to doubt even his truthfulness, leading to enmity.
key_terms.الْمَاجِنُ: The immoral or pious-but-lacking-depth person who focuses on outward deeds but lacks depth in religion and hereafter.

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people a Muslim should avoid befriending according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) advised Muslims to avoid close companionship with three types of people: the immoral who lack religious commitment, the foolish who cannot convey good or ward off evil, and the liar whose frequent storytelling destroys trust and sows enmity. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, highlights the Shia emphasis on *mu'akhah* (close companionship) as a spiritual safeguard, warning that even well-meaning fools can cause harm, while liars distort truth and breed hidden hostility. The advice underscores the practical need for discernment in social circles to preserve one's faith and inner peace.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Amro Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Salim Al Kindy, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘It was so that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> ascended the Pulpit, said: ‘It is befitting for the Muslim that he keeps aside from establishing brotherhood with three – the immoral, and the stupid, and the liar.

So, as for the immoral, so he would adorn his deed for you and he would love it if you could become like him, and he will not assist you upon the matter of your Religion and your Hereafter; and associating with him is disloyalty and hard-heartedness, and his entry and his exit is a disgrace upon you.

And as for the stupid, so he would not indicate upon you with the good, nor would he hope for the exchanging of the evil from you and even if he has to fight against his own self; and sometimes he intends to benefit you, but (instead) he harms you. Thus, his death is better than his life, and his silence is better than his speaking, and his remoteness is better than his nearness.

And as for the liar, so life is not welcoming with him. He transmits your narration and transmist the narration to you. Everytime he runs out of a narration, so he stretches it with another to the extent that when he does narrate with the truth, he is not believed; and he entices the people with the enmity, so he cause the grudges to grown in the chests.
Therefore, fear Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> and look out for yourselves!’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn Salim al-Kendi from those who narrated to him from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) from the pulpit would say, ‘It is very proper for a Muslim not to establish brotherhood with three kinds of people: a vulgar, a silly or a lying person;

a vulgar person polishes his acts for you and loves that you become like him. He does not help you in your religious matters and your life in the hereafter. Association with him is injustice and hardheartedness. His coming and going with you is a disgrace.

“A silly person does not show you anything good. There is no hope in his diverting any evil from you even if he may make an effort to help. Perhaps he may like to benefit you, instead he harms you. His death is better than his living, his silence is better than speaking, and his being at a distance is better than his being nearby.

“You can never have a happy life with a lying person. He narrates your words to others and the words of the others to you. Whenever he runs out of a story, he stretches one story to the other so much so that even if he may tell the truth it is not believed. He creates animosity among people and grows hatred in the hearts.
Be pious before Allah and look after your souls.’”
